world.setting: a waterfront house in Annapolis, Maryland; a garden club; a quiet winter
world.register: intimate, wry, slow; a woman writing to be heard

felix.look: a man in his late forties, lean, neat short hair, button-down shirt, 2012 clothing

harry.name: Harry

harry.look: a young man in his twenties, hoodie, messy hair, jeans, 2012 clothing

kitchen.look: a quiet kitchen with a mug of tea and dishes drying by the sink

court.look: a courtroom where Sybil once argued, dense legal files on the table

objects.why: the letters and emails the whole book is made of
decades of briefs and judicial opinions, the old discipline
the isolated waterfront house, a life lived alone
divorced mother, grandmother, the people she writes to
the river and the frozen shore outside her window
the garden club and its petty turf wars
a grief memoir she hides in a drawer
what she risks when she finally writes something true

spine.claim: Sybil lives alone in Annapolis, and writing is the only way she still speaks to the world.
Her garden club feud and her long-distance letters show her power over people is really a power over words.
A new correspondence reaches her, and she starts to reveal more of herself than she plans to.
Letters she never sends carry the grief she does not say aloud.
The book asks what a reader would miss if they saw only the messages a person chose to send.
